associations.rationale: The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: The endomorphism ring of a finite-dimensional module satisfying the ambient module condition is local.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Any two simple modules over a simple Artinian ring are linearly equivalent.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: The diagonal matrix units form a complete family of orthogonal idempotents.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: The coordinate-supported diagonal matrix units form a complete family of orthogonal idempotents in a finite product.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: The coordinate units form a complete family of orthogonal idempotents in a finite product of semirings.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: An auxiliary statement whose displayed formal type is unavailable.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: A finite nontrivial module over an Artinian ring has a coatom among its submodules.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: For an exhaustive finite family of simple modules, every finite nontrivial module determines an index together with a nonzero map.

The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: For a finite pairwise nonisomorphic family of simple modules, there are pairwise orthogonal idempotents whose associated submodules have Kronecker-delta dimensions.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: For an idempotent, the dimension of the space of linear maps from its cyclic submodule equals the dimension of the associated submodule.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: The cyclic submodules generated by a complete family of orthogonal idempotents form an internal direct sum.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Conjugate elements generate linearly equivalent cyclic submodules.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: The cyclic submodule generated by one element of a ring is finite over that ring.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: An idempotent whose linear-map dimensions select one simple module has a cyclic submodule satisfying the designated module property.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: The cyclic submodule generated by an idempotent is projective.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Sandwiching a matrix by a diagonal matrix unit extracts its corresponding diagonal entry.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: A diagonal matrix unit is an idempotent element.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Coordinate-supported elements built from idempotents form an orthogonal family in a finite product.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: A coordinate unit commutes with every element of a finite product of semirings.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Associates a linear endomorphism over the base field to an element acting on a module.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Associates a submodule over the base field to an element acting on a module.
The formal type directly states or defines the item: An auxiliary statement whose displayed formal type contains an elided term.

The formal type directly states or defines the item: A family of finite projective modules with Kronecker-delta linear-map dimensions decomposes the regular module as a direct sum with multiplicities given by the dimensions of the simple modules.

The formal type directly states or defines the item: Every finite projective module satisfying the designated module property is linearly equivalent to a member of a projective family with Kronecker-delta linear-map dimensions.

The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: An endomorphism of a finite-dimensional module satisfying the designated module property is nilpotent when its range lies in a proper submodule.

The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Two finite-dimensional projective modules satisfying the designated module property are linearly equivalent if both admit nonzero maps to the same simple module.
